candidates.title: Shared production builds expose colocated test modules
candidates.problemSummary: A normal shared build emits 73 colocated test suites beside production modules, and 69 acquire valid wildcard package subpaths. Accidental test exposure is indistinguishable from the deliberate test-helper export.
candidates.directionSummary: Use a production emitting project that excludes colocated suites while retaining the intentional test helper export and a separate no-emit test type-check path.

candidates.title: Saving-throw phases exchange oversized and independently derived state
candidates.problemSummary: The staged saving-throw API's phase boundaries do not express the data each phase needs, so callers carry large parallel input/check structures. One logical saving throw ends up with two unlinked sources of truth across shared rules and the server spell-resolution service.
candidates.directionSummary: Introduce focused check and resolution inputs, making the check own its DC/modifier or recomputing derived state from natural rolls so incoherent pairs are unrepresentable.

candidates.title: Five summary projections hand-copy canonical entity fields
candidates.problemSummary: Five summary schemas maintain 33 parallel field declarations copied from canonical entity schemas. Multiple copies have already drifted from their canonical validators.
candidates.directionSummary: Derive summaries with entitySchema.pick(...).extend(...), making any deliberately looser projection explicit in the extend step with a rationale.

candidates.title: Encounter inputs are a monolith spanning three router boundaries
candidates.problemSummary: One 329-line, 20-schema contract module mixes CRUD, state transitions, participants, turns, combat logs, and combat-map integration. Independent router work is forced onto one high-churn file that does not mirror the server's stable boundaries.
candidates.directionSummary: Split contracts along the existing encounter, encounter-combat, and encounter-map boundaries, moving consumers atomically and extracting only genuinely shared fields into neutral fragments.

candidates.title: spellcasting.ts contains five independently changing rule areas
candidates.problemSummary: Caster resolution, slot progression, prepared limits, cantrip fallback policy, and character-creation selection all converge on one 380-line file. Its broad name no longer identifies a useful review or navigation boundary.
candidates.directionSummary: Split along the existing section boundaries, keeping each rule table beside the logic that interprets it and avoiding compatibility barrels.

candidates.title: attack-damage.ts is an eight-concern rules grab bag
candidates.problemSummary: Eight distinct concerns (property normalization, ability selection, weapon/spell bonuses, inventory translation, aggregation, proficiency policy, formatting) accumulated in one file. The boundary reflects history rather than stable rule concepts.
candidates.directionSummary: Split around weapon calculation, inventory adaptation, spellcasting-derived values, and formatting/proficiency, retaining direct concrete subpath imports.

candidates.title: Sorcery mechanics and the metamagic content catalog are tangled
candidates.problemSummary: An 82-line metamagic display/content catalog sits in the middle of the sorcery-point mechanics module. Content-copy and mechanical-rule changes share a module and conflict unnecessarily.
candidates.directionSummary: Move the metamagic option catalog and identity lookup into a focused content module, keeping sorcery-point and combination mechanics in the rules module.

candidates.title: Monster provenance invariants disappear from the inferred contract
candidates.problemSummary: Monster-source mutual exclusion and homebrew id/version pairing live only in a superRefine that does not narrow z.infer. The inferred type admits states the parser rejects, and the separately exported monster schema bypasses the invariant entirely.
candidates.directionSummary: Model custom, SRD, and homebrew sources as structural Zod union variants that preserve wire keys while making exclusion and id/version correlation visible to z.infer.

candidates.title: Condition and damage modules mix contracts, persistence repair, and rules
candidates.problemSummary: Condition and damage modules simultaneously own vocabulary, Zod contracts, persisted-data repair, and executable rules. A type-only bidirectional dependency between rules and the encounter schema obscures dependency direction and concept ownership.
candidates.directionSummary: Create one-way leaf modules for condition/damage contracts and persisted-value normalization, leaving executable behavior in rules and preserving tolerant read behavior.

candidates.title: Shared weapon rules helpers demand full entities and force server double assertions
candidates.problemSummary: getWeaponDataFromItem and related attack-damage rules helpers demand complete wire entities (a full InventoryItem) while reading only a few fields. This forces the server's focused Prisma projection in resolve-attack.ts through documented unknown-to-InventoryItem double assertions and couples unrelated schema changes to attack resolution, with the same over-demanding inputs also constraining client consumers like equipment-summary.
candidates.directionSummary: Define focused structural helper inputs containing only the used fields (itemType, name, unknown properties), retain weaponPropertiesSchema.safeParse at the boundary, derive the server participant shape from its Prisma selection, and remove the assertion bridges.

candidates.title: One metamagic constant controls two unrelated rule limits
candidates.problemSummary: Cast input validation uses METAMAGIC_PICKS_PER_LEVEL as its per-cast cap even though MAX_METAMAGIC_PER_CAST is the semantically distinct quantity. Changing how many options are learned would silently change per-cast limits.
candidates.directionSummary: Export and consume a separately named per-cast limit, confining the milestone-pick constant to level-up selection.

candidates.title: Attack and spell contracts duplicate behavior-bearing field validators
candidates.problemSummary: Attack and spell-action contracts privately duplicate the same bonus bounds, dice-notation, and combat-name validators. Notation or bound changes require coordinated edits and can silently diverge.
candidates.directionSummary: Move the shared field schemas and semantically shared bounds into a neutral combat-contract fragment consumed by both families.

candidates.title: Encounter calculators re-declare the participant discriminator twice
candidates.problemSummary: DifficultyParticipant and XpParticipant hand-write the canonical three-member participant discriminator with no type relationship to the contract. Adding or renaming a kind requires coordinated edits TypeScript cannot connect.
candidates.directionSummary: Derive calculator inputs from a small canonical participant contract, or type their discriminator through a dependency-safe leaf schema.

candidates.title: The attunement game rule lives in a request-schema module
candidates.problemSummary: MAX_ATTUNED_ITEMS, the authoritative attunement business rule driving service enforcement and two UI surfaces, is declared among request bounds no schema in the file uses. Unrelated consumers are coupled to transport contracts.
candidates.directionSummary: Move the constant into an inventory rules/vocabulary module and repoint service and UI consumers atomically.

candidates.title: Campaign-homebrew procedure contracts are split by input versus output
candidates.problemSummary: homebrew-campaign.ts is a tiny output-only module with no entity or vocabulary justifying the split. Following one procedure requires discovering its input and output halves in two files.
candidates.directionSummary: Co-locate the outputs with their matching request contracts, or rename and document a genuinely independent campaign-link contract boundary.

candidates.title: The shared package exports 122 types with no non-test adopter
candidates.problemSummary: Of 422 exported type/interface declarations, 122 have no occurrence outside their own declaration in non-test code. The declaration surface looks like a supported API and obscures genuinely shared types.
candidates.directionSummary: Prune the measured aliases by domain, retaining runtime schemas and consumed types, and require an adopter in the same change for future named aliases.

candidates.title: Weapon helpers widen closed vocabularies back to string
candidates.problemSummary: The weapon pipeline models closed WeaponCategory and DamageTypeName vocabularies, then discards their precision at the next helper boundaries (string damageType, Record<string,string> category map, string proficiency input). Coverage enforcement is lost.
candidates.directionSummary: Use Record<WeaponCategory,string>, accept WeaponCategory in proficiency checks, and preserve DamageTypeName in WeaponAttackResult.

candidates.title: Combat result schemas make an always-produced roll mode optional
candidates.problemSummary: attackResolutionResultSchema and savingThrowResultSchema declare rollMode optional even though the canonical D20 producers always supply it. Consumers are forced to handle an absent state these flows never produce.
candidates.directionSummary: Make rollMode required in both result schemas after inventorying non-canonical persisted producers, retaining optionality only for second-roll fields.

candidates.title: Static rules tables expose inconsistent mutability contracts
candidates.problemSummary: Uppercase exports of immutable reference data are sometimes mutable arrays/records while neighboring tables are readonly. The public type surface communicates inconsistent invariants.
candidates.directionSummary: Expose readonly rows, records, and arrays consistently while preserving intentional tolerant lookup signatures.

candidates.title: Dice grammar semantics depend on positional regex captures
candidates.problemSummary: Dice parsing relies on four positional capture groups indexed as match[1]..match[4] plus an asserted keep discriminator, so grammar edits must keep parentheses, indexes, conversions, and the asserted union manually synchronized. The assertion is also mislabeled as framework typing.
candidates.directionSummary: Use named capture groups or a typed match-decoding helper and classify any unavoidable assertion as an interop boundary.

candidates.title: Responsive character sheets keep two independent component trees alive
candidates.problemSummary: SheetBody always mounts both desktop and mobile layouts (14 panel types instantiated twice) with CSS hiding one. State can diverge across breakpoints and hook/render work is duplicated.
candidates.directionSummary: Render one stateful panel tree with responsive placement, or select one layout through a browser-media boundary, preserving SheetSharedProps.

candidates.title: The VTT Actions tab duplicates two dedicated tabs and has already drifted
candidates.problemSummary: The compact Actions surface reimplements the spell and feature records of the dedicated tabs with divergent eligibility and mutation behavior. It has already produced contradictory production controls.
candidates.directionSummary: Split into spell and feature slices that share pure row/view models and focused row primitives between compact and full presentations.

candidates.title: Character hooks expose a second identity channel beside their cache scope
candidates.problemSummary: Nine character-scoped hooks capture characterId for cache scope yet their actions accept another characterId through raw RPC inputs. Mutation targeting can disagree with optimistic-update or invalidation scope.
candidates.directionSummary: Expose id-free domain payloads and inject the captured characterId inside each hook, migrating by domain without identity brands.

candidates.title: Optimistic writers spread transport envelopes into cached domain objects
candidates.problemSummary: Three optimistic writers use incompatible conventions for separating transport control data from persisted entity data. Future authorization or concurrency fields can silently enter cached rows without compiler feedback.
candidates.directionSummary: Give each writer a positive, typed domain-patch projection, keeping identifiers, authorization scope, and CAS tokens outside cached entity patches.

candidates.title: The flat character-creation contract forces manual two-way state adapters
candidates.problemSummary: The wizard reducer stores a flattened submission projection while steps reconstruct richer editing state. This requires paired local/reducer writes, whole-slice payloads, and bidirectional conversion helpers whose correctness depends on every handler preserving unrelated fields.
candidates.directionSummary: Model typed per-step drafts and fine-grained events with one authoritative state owner per editing model, deriving the transport projection at submission.

candidates.title: Character-creation ability rules have four independent sources of truth
candidates.problemSummary: Editing, validation, review, and submission each duplicate the point-buy table, standard array, ability metadata, modifier math, or boost aggregation with no type-level relationship. The four surfaces can drift independently.
candidates.directionSummary: Create one pure character-creation ability model for constants, score/boost derivation, modifiers, and validation, keeping step modules presentational.

candidates.title: The generic map canvas performs combat-domain adaptation
candidates.problemSummary: The low-level map renderer imports EncounterDetail and derives combat state (turn order, HP, conditions, participant identity). It changes with encounter contracts and contradicts the documented feature boundary assigning combat behavior to ../combat.
candidates.directionSummary: Build a render-oriented combat-token lookup in the combat feature and pass it to MapCanvas; ordinary maps pass no combat projection.

candidates.title: ToolHandler erases coordinate domains and invents fake capabilities
candidates.problemSummary: The tool-handler abstraction pairs a runtime coordinateSpace flag with structurally identical callbacks so pixel/cell mismatches type-check. It forces no-op onStart members and splits interaction semantics across two registries.
candidates.directionSummary: Use a discriminated descriptor union for pixel, cell, cancellation-only, and overlay-managed tools with interaction behavior encoded in the descriptor.

candidates.title: Encounter detail behavior is fragmented across presentation files
candidates.problemSummary: Changing one encounter action requires discovering behavior across a 384-line composition view, a hook hidden in a row file, and raw mutation objects threaded through presentation. No single controller owns the encounter-detail mutation surface.
candidates.directionSummary: Create an encounter-detail controller module for mutation construction, concurrency payloads, invalidation, and pending state, exposing narrow intent callbacks to readable sections.

candidates.title: Participant presentation is duplicated between encounter setup and combat
candidates.problemSummary: State-independent participant identity, statistics, and visibility have two independent markup/styling vocabularies. The generic primitives are filed under combat, encouraging setup code to reproduce them.
candidates.directionSummary: Move state-independent participant primitives to a neutral encounter-participant module and compose setup-only and combat-only controls around them.

candidates.title: The monster editor's sections share one 47-field flat state boundary
candidates.problemSummary: MonsterFormData's 47 flat fields span six domains with every section able to read or mutate every field. Field additions require coordinated changes through two 400-plus-line adapter modules.
candidates.directionSummary: Introduce domain sub-form types with narrow section props for each domain and split the adapters along the same boundaries.

candidates.title: The flat route tree makes authentication an eleven-site convention
candidates.problemSummary: Authentication is encoded by 11 copied per-route AuthGuard wrappers rather than route hierarchy. Protected-area ownership is invisible in route-tree.ts and adding a route requires a per-file ritual.
candidates.directionSummary: Introduce one pathless authenticated parent route rendering AuthGuard around an Outlet and reparent protected routes beneath it.

candidates.title: SettingsPage implements three account features behind a nominal page boundary
candidates.problemSummary: Profile editing, password rotation, and account deletion are fully implemented inside one 332-line route file with no discoverable feature home. This contradicts the page module's composition-boundary contract.
candidates.directionSummary: Move the three workflows into focused account/settings components and hooks, leaving SettingsPage as the route-facing composition root.

candidates.title: Campaign tabs are manually synchronized across three registries
candidates.problemSummary: Eight campaign tabs are declared in separate trigger and content registries plus a route union. A documentation checklist compensates for the missing structural guarantee that each tab has one trigger, one panel, and aligned access policy.
candidates.directionSummary: Define an exhaustive page-local Record<CampaignTab, descriptor> for label, icon, access, and panel rendering, deriving triggers and contents from it.

candidates.title: FilterSelect erases schema-derived option types
candidates.problemSummary: The shared FilterSelect widens values, option values, and callbacks to string across 12 call sites. Consumers are forced to recover their literal unions through casts and assertion-boundary comments.
candidates.directionSummary: Make FilterSelect generic over its option-value union and represent the all-selection sentinel explicitly.

candidates.title: MonsterAddData erases mutually exclusive monster origins
candidates.problemSummary: MonsterAddData models SRD and homebrew origins as unrelated optional fields permitting neither, both, or versions without entries. Three converters independently repeat the common participant defaults.
candidates.directionSummary: Use a discriminated SRD-versus-homebrew origin plus common stats, centralize source adapters, and flatten only at the mutation boundary.

candidates.title: TokenContextMenu is an option bag for two different surfaces
candidates.problemSummary: One partially configured component serves base map editing and combat with fourteen props including seven optional combat values coordinated by isInCombat. Its type admits combat branches without their required callbacks.
candidates.directionSummary: Use explicit map and combat variants or a discriminated props union that requires the complete combat contract while sharing invariant menu items locally.

candidates.title: Player and monster attack hooks duplicate the target-pick lifecycle
candidates.problemSummary: Two hooks independently own the same stateful target-pick interaction protocol (load, eligibility, activation, invalidation, drawer restoration). Cleanup and eligibility behavior can drift with each additional attack mode.
candidates.directionSummary: Extract an internal attack-targeting coordinator for the shared lifecycle, keeping typed payload construction in adapters.

candidates.title: Token placement mirrors store state into dialog state through an indirect effect
candidates.problemSummary: A setter wrapper passed into usePlacementSlice hides a synchronous derived-state effect from the lint rule. This creates two sources of truth that every dialog close path must coordinate.
candidates.directionSummary: Remove the opening callback and derive dialog visibility from manualAddOpen or a non-null placement cell, keeping pending-cell clearing in close/success handlers.

candidates.title: Homebrew entry-type vocabulary is enumerated across parallel client and shared registries
candidates.problemSummary: The homebrew entry-type vocabulary is repeated across the shared enum, schema record, client form typing, the editor registry, an entry-dialog selector list, an entry-card label map, and non-exhaustive create/filter option arrays. Only the implementation registry is compiler-enforced, so adding a type can compile while silently missing its selector, labels, plurals, or filters, making its editor unreachable.
candidates.directionSummary: Establish one exhaustive client entry-type metadata registry keyed by HomebrewEntryType owning labels, order, plurals, and filter/creation options, deriving selector, card, and filter surfaces from it, while keeping validation schemas in shared and retaining the separately typed editor binding registry.

candidates.title: RollModeToggle is a complete production-orphan component
candidates.problemSummary: A 60-line UI component has zero production imports across 389 pinned production client files. Its implementation, test presence, and module listing make it appear to be an active combat surface.
candidates.directionSummary: Remove the orphan production component; L07-106 (D-110) owns the misleading MODULE entry and lane 06 owns the test-only surface.

candidates.title: Character key hook constructs three filter objects no production caller reads
candidates.problemSummary: useCharacterKeys builds characterFilter, spellsFilter, and inventoryFilter (plus their QueryFilter type) on every call, but all nine production consumers read only the exact keys. An abandoned invalidation API enlarges a central cache-key contract.
candidates.directionSummary: Delete the three filter members and the unused QueryFilter interface, leaving useCharacterKeys focused on its three consumed exact keys; L07-108 (D-112) owns the comment correction.

candidates.title: Server service suites redundantly wipe the database 119 times
candidates.problemSummary: The global server test lifecycle already resets the worker database, yet fifteen service suites repeat cleanDb in their own hooks (119 calls, 22 deletes each). Ownership of isolation is unclear and focused runs pay for thousands of unnecessary deletes.
candidates.directionSummary: Remove redundant per-suite resets, keep only suites that intentionally mutate state outside the shared lifecycle, and document those exceptions beside the hook.

candidates.title: A legacy invite suite duplicates the newer split suites
candidates.problemSummary: The old monolithic invite suite survived after behavior was split into focused manage/join files; 16 of 17 cases overlap. Duplicate setup and assertions obscure which suite is authoritative.
candidates.directionSummary: Move the one unique URL-extraction case into invite-join.test.ts and delete the legacy suite.

candidates.title: Encounter map behavior is duplicated across two large router suites
candidates.problemSummary: Procedure contracts and encounter-level integration are mixed in both files, giving two partially overlapping authorities for the same map behavior (about twelve repeated contracts). Repeated failure cases also exist within one file.
candidates.directionSummary: Keep procedure/authorization contracts in encounter-map.test.ts, retain only mapId integration in encounter-combat-map.test.ts, and remove weaker duplicates.

candidates.title: wizard-context.test.tsx is a stale duplicate of wizard-state coverage
candidates.problemSummary: A context-named 27-case suite never tests the context boundary, duplicates the newer 69-case reducer suite, and carries stale step semantics. Contributors get two conflicting descriptions of the wizard.
candidates.directionSummary: Delete the duplicate suite or replace it with a small provider/hook integration contract for the actual context facade.

candidates.title: character-sheet.test.tsx no longer tests a character-sheet composition
candidates.problemSummary: The filename promises composition coverage but the file is an outdated aggregate of leaf-component tests already covered beside their subjects. It adds churn while concealing the real page-level layout authority.
candidates.directionSummary: Prune duplicate leaf describes and retain only focused coverage for components lacking colocated tests.

candidates.title: Optimistic character-sheet mutations omit consumer-level rollback contracts
candidates.problemSummary: The restore helper is tested in isolation, but the mutation-option bindings choosing which snapshot is restored and which queries are invalidated are not (seven onError branches and eight settled invalidation paths untested). Wiring can be dropped without a focused failure.
candidates.directionSummary: Use the existing failing-mutation seam to assert optimistic state, exact rollback, and both invalidation families per mutation shape, replacing shell assertions.

candidates.title: VTT spell tests copy full CharacterSpellWithDetails payloads
candidates.problemSummary: Six VTT drawer files define 18 raw CharacterSpellWithDetails objects (407 lines, four exact Fireball copies). Schema changes become multi-file edits and case intent is buried in invariant payload fields.
candidates.directionSummary: Add a typed spell-scenario builder with a canonical default, keeping local semantic names and explicit overrides.

candidates.title: map-inputs tests obscure mutations inside repeated payload literals
candidates.problemSummary: An 895-line suite repeats near-identical payload literals (mapId 55 times, zero-coordinate fields 23 times each). Schema evolution produces broad edits and reviewers must diff whole payloads to find the field under test.
candidates.directionSummary: Introduce file-local z.input-typed bases/builders for create-map, create-token, and move-token inputs with labeled tables for symmetric boundaries.

candidates.title: Two drift advisories duplicate the complete bounded-history fixture
candidates.problemSummary: A large evolving analyzer contract fixture (60 lines) is hand-copied in two advisory suites. A harmless BoundedFullHistory field addition requires synchronized edits and each advisory's actual inputs are hidden.
candidates.directionSummary: Extract a focused test helper for commit records, changes, and bounded-history defaults.

candidates.title: Drift-AI suites leave dozens of temporary repositories behind
candidates.problemSummary: Six drift-AI files create roughly 58 unremoved temporary roots per full run. Suites reimplement only the allocation half of lifecycle management despite an existing shared cleanup helper.
candidates.directionSummary: Route these suites through registerTempRootCleanup, keeping raw mkdtempSync only where a test explicitly owns a distinct lifecycle.

candidates.title: Eight drift command fakes bypass the strict Git helper
candidates.problemSummary: Command tests use two incompatible Git-fake styles; eight lenient stubs across six files silently tolerate wrong or added Git calls. Those suites are poor documentation of their dependency contract.
candidates.directionSummary: Use the strict currentRepoGit helper with explicit local extensions only for intentionally permitted commands.

candidates.title: Drift baseline tests repeatedly rebuild immutable expensive fixtures
candidates.problemSummary: Assertions request identical corpus discovery 11 times and rebuild the same committed Git baseline six times. The suites are heavier than needed and it is unclear which cases actually need fresh state.
candidates.directionSummary: Share immutable evaluated corpus results within describes and use a prepared committed baseline for admission scenarios, keeping one fidelity test and the independent determinism check.

candidates.title: triage-report tests bury scenarios in repeated envelope boilerplate
candidates.problemSummary: Most of the 1,144-line suite repeats transport envelopes (25 schemaVersion, 15 advisory, 13-14 copies of each empty metadata array) rather than the one triage mutation each case exercises. Contract changes create broad edits.
candidates.directionSummary: Add typed driftInput, semgrepInput, dolosInput, and row builders while keeping malformed-contract cases as explicit raw objects.

candidates.title: Codemod fixtures duplicate identical before and after trees
candidates.problemSummary: 35 of 90 codemod cases carry byte-identical before/after trees (44 duplicate files, about 324 lines), doubling fixture review surface without adding an oracle. Runners encode unchanged cases inconsistently.
candidates.directionSummary: Move the missing-after fallback into the shared fixture helper and remove byte-identical after trees, keeping explicit after trees where output differs.

candidates.title: ESLint configuration suites repeat real-repository harness plumbing
candidates.problemSummary: Ten suites independently reconstruct the same repository ESLint instance and small query helpers (five repeat configFor, five severityOf). Configuration changes fan out and repeated setup obscures each suite's policy assertion.
candidates.directionSummary: Extract a resolved-eslint-config test helper for root/path/ESLint construction and common queries, leaving suites and assertions in place.

candidates.title: Portable lint-ratchet tests depend on privileged directory symlinks
candidates.problemSummary: Five test files in a package intended to be portable create node_modules directory symlinks. That is a host privilege commonly unavailable to new Windows contributors without Developer Mode or admin rights.
candidates.directionSummary: Use a junction where appropriate or inject dependency resolution so fixture repositories can borrow installed dependencies without privileged directory symlinks.

candidates.title: Server mutation Vitest config re-declares the regular server lifecycle
candidates.problemSummary: The mutation config independently repeats the server test lifecycle and environment fields. Routine changes to setup, workers, or database semantics require synchronized edits in two configs with no parity guard.
candidates.directionSummary: Extract plain shared server test options/constants while keeping deliberate mutation differences local.

candidates.title: Utility and broadcast tests seed through character-create service internals
candidates.problemSummary: Lower-level mapper and socket-contract tests import character-create service internals for setup (the seed pair repeated nine times). This reverses the intended test dependency and broadens unrelated refactor fallout.
candidates.directionSummary: Use a low-level typed Prisma fixture or the public character test helper for setup, reserving real service-path seeding for service-workflow tests.

candidates.title: E2E specs bypass page objects through raw selectors and public locators
candidates.problemSummary: 25 raw getBy* calls in six specs and at least 18 direct public locator-field accesses give specs and page objects two competing automation idioms. UI refactors require editing narratives instead of one page-object contract.
candidates.directionSummary: Add atomic page-object methods for named wizard boosts and Continue-state assertions, then migrate the highest-value raw call sites without splitting encounter-combat.

candidates.title: Two command test filenames substantially overstate their coverage
candidates.problemSummary: Both filenames imply command-level coverage but the suites test only regexes/helpers, omitting traversal, output/exit behavior, worker validation, report construction, and CLI parsing. Contributors can assume operational contracts exist when they do not.
candidates.directionSummary: Rename the files as core/helper suites and add small injected-runner or fixture-repository command contracts for the operational boundaries.

candidates.title: Eleven non-encounter E2E suites present shared-state narratives as 77 separate tests
candidates.problemSummary: Eleven whole-describe serial groups contain 77 tests that are really dependent workflow steps. Later cases cannot run alone, earlier failures suppress remaining contracts, and prerequisites are conveyed only by source order.
candidates.directionSummary: Represent genuinely sequential workflows as scenarios with named steps and independently seed contracts via fixtures/API helpers before removing serialization, leaving encounter-combat unchanged.

candidates.title: Pagination suites systematically avoid the tie cases their cursors must disambiguate
candidates.problemSummary: Five pagination authorities (1,385 lines) build fixtures with unique cursor keys by construction and contain zero equal-order-key page-boundary cases. Cursor composition can regress by skipping or duplicating equal-key records while all assertions stay green.
candidates.directionSummary: For each endpoint, seed multiple pages with rows sharing the boundary sort tuple, traverse until nextCursor is null, and assert the exact expected ID set.

candidates.title: Three mutation-test lanes can strand live source mutations after interruption
candidates.problemSummary: Three in-place Stryker lanes write mutants into the contributor's active worktree; a kill or crash can mix stranded mutations with legitimate uncommitted work. The command surface has no stale-state detection or safe recovery rail.
candidates.directionSummary: Run in-place lanes in automatically provisioned disposable worktrees, or add a supervised runner that snapshots targets, detects stale backups, and restores safely.

candidates.title: Multi-artifact harness generators lack a failure-and-recovery test contract
candidates.problemSummary: Generator tests prove final bytes only when every write succeeds; none exercise a mid-batch write failure. Whether earlier outputs stay updated, how check mode reports mixed generations, or whether rerun repairs them is undefined.
candidates.directionSummary: Put batch orchestration behind an injectable writer and add boundary-failure cases asserting error propagation, stale-output detection, scratch cleanup, and repair on rerun.

candidates.title: Coverage gates count 490 lines of test scaffolding as product code
candidates.problemSummary: Nine test-support modules totaling 490 lines are included in coverage denominators and easily exercised numerators. Coverage can rise or hold steady without more production behavior being covered, making the advertised thresholds hard to interpret.

candidates.title: Enable the existing comment-density sensor for scripts with narrow exceptions
candidates.problemSummary: The comment-density check wholesale-excludes scripts and eslint-rules, hiding 570 tooling files from automated signal. The detector and report-only calibration already exist.
candidates.directionSummary: Replace the blanket exclusions with a small list of generated, vendored, or deliberately prose-heavy exceptions, initially keeping advisory behavior.

candidates.title: Shared runtime-neutrality enforcement permits Node dependencies
candidates.problemSummary: The shared package's runtime-neutrality policy blocks browser/framework dependencies but not Node builtins or globals, and its tsconfig grants Node ambient types. Server-only dependencies can compile and lint unnoticed; production code is currently clean so enforcement has no migration debt.
candidates.directionSummary: Ban Node builtins and Node-only globals in production shared files, keeping Node types for test-only configurations or sentinel exclusions and preserving existing browser restrictions.

candidates.title: Worktree provisioning is hard-wired to devcontainer credentials despite the root Compose setup
candidates.problemSummary: worktree-db.sh's admin_url unconditionally requires .devcontainer/.env, so a contributor on the root Compose stack with valid credentials cannot provision. Mechanically copying the devcontainer file selects the container-only db:5432 hostname.
candidates.directionSummary: Give admin_url an explicit credential-source contract: a dedicated worktree-admin override, devcontainer compatibility, and root .env support when it is the active topology, validating the URL before writes and aligning L07-017 (D-101) documentation.

candidates.title: Add a preview/apply safety boundary to SRD backfills
candidates.problemSummary: Database-writing SRD backfill commands connect and mutate immediately with no target confirmation, preview mode, or change-count summary. A wrong environment is observable only after writes begin.
candidates.directionSummary: Have the common runner print a sanitized host/database target, require an explicit apply flag, and add dry-run summaries to both callbacks, choosing transaction semantics separately.

candidates.title: Let lint-ratchet proposal previews evaluate third-party rules
candidates.problemSummary: The proposal command supports only core and local rule kinds, rejecting third-party rule ids. Adopters must hand-author allowlist, source shape, parser profile, and registry entry before previewing — defeating the safe-preview purpose.
candidates.directionSummary: Add plugin identity and parser-profile proposal options validated against the injected binding and allowlist, constructing the existing third-party source shape and emitting a promotable registry entry.

candidates.title: Homebrew write validation loses its type correlation before editor reads
candidates.problemSummary: Shared and server correlate homebrew type with its data schema during validation but reads expose Record<string, unknown>. Eight client getDefault adapters each rebuild partial decoders from opaque persisted records.
candidates.directionSummary: Expose a shared typed read adapter or discriminated persisted-entry union derived from the existing registry, migrating the eight adapters incrementally while preserving deliberately separate form-state coercions.

candidates.title: Downstream packages keep semantic copies beside shared rule authorities
candidates.problemSummary: Shared authorities (RollMode, MAX_SPELL_LEVEL, template size, monster spell frequencies, CR rules) have semantic copies in server and client — or live in undiscoverable attack-specific modules — that can drift independently across package boundaries.
candidates.directionSummary: Move RollMode to a neutral d20 contract, import shared constants and frequency tuples directly, relocate CR-to-proficiency beside shared CR-to-XP, and add a narrow semantic-straggler check rather than a general constants package.

candidates.title: Make combat history navigable through one paginated read model
candidates.problemSummary: Encounter detail always loads the full unbounded combat-log relation which the UI ignores, while the visible panel shows only the paginated API's first 50 records with no continuation control. Later history is unreachable in long encounters.
candidates.directionSummary: Remove logs from EncounterDetail and its unbounded include, make listCombatLogs the sole read model, and give the panel an infinite-query or load-more flow with an explicit initial-page ordering policy.

candidates.title: Turn the disabled stat-block placeholder into a party reveal workflow
candidates.problemSummary: Players cannot inspect discovered creatures because stat-block access is DM-only and all-or-nothing. DMs are forced to relay statistics through chat despite an existing reusable renderer and a disabled placeholder action.
candidates.directionSummary: Persist per-participant reveal state, broadcast it through the existing encounter update path, and add a spectator-safe drawer mode hiding HP and mutation controls, keeping reveal distinct from token visibility.

candidates.title: Let players choose Strength or Dexterity for Finesse attacks
candidates.problemSummary: The shared rule silently picks the better Strength/Dexterity modifier for Finesse weapons even though the SRD rule text grants the attacker the choice. The attack input contract has no ability-choice field.
candidates.directionSummary: Add an optional server-validated Strength-or-Dexterity override for Finesse weapons, keeping best-modifier as default and showing a compact selector only when both choices are legal.

candidates.title: Expose the level-up history already returned with each character
candidates.problemSummary: Character detail already returns structured levelChoices history, but zero production client consumers exist. Players must reconstruct prior class, subclass, feat, and ability choices from the sheet or external notes.
candidates.directionSummary: Render a read-only level timeline grouped by level with human-readable labels, treating rollback as separate future design since the records lack a reversible mutation manifest.

candidates.title: Baseline updates serialize stale local toolchain state into repository-wide hash churn
candidates.problemSummary: Ordinary debt-floor updates serialize ruleSourceHash identities derived from the caller's installed dependency tree. A stale installation rewrites most of the baseline — a real occurrence already required a corrective revert.
candidates.directionSummary: Verify the installed toolchain against the lockfile before writing, reject dependency-driven hash-only churn with a focused recovery message, and separate intentional identity refreshes from debt-floor updates.

candidates.title: The portable lint-ratchet package hard-codes Musi's operational vocabulary
candidates.problemSummary: The reusable kernel and governance layers embed Musi's baseline filename and bun run commands (11 references across 5 kernel files). Adopters must edit package source and a Musi command rename is a multi-surface change.
candidates.directionSummary: Introduce one workflow-presentation binding for filenames and update/install/restore commands, or move all host-facing remediation prose into the adapter.

candidates.title: The public lint-ratchet demo asks adopters to maintain a 1,245-line fork
candidates.problemSummary: The reusable package stops below the operational adoption seam: outside repositories must vendor 1,245 lines of CLI parsing, merge-driver management, recovery, and preflight wrappers while the actual demo application is 17 lines.
candidates.directionSummary: Ship supported package executables or a versioned bootstrap generator for the operational rail, leaving adopters one registry/binding file and optional renderers.

candidates.title: Rule-source hashing depends on a home-grown JavaScript import lexer
candidates.problemSummary: Source-identity correctness rests on a 445-line bespoke regex-based import lexer and masking guard with unusual formatting restrictions. New syntax support is risky and the code is hard to present as a reusable reference.
candidates.directionSummary: Use the already-declared TypeScript parser API to enumerate static imports/exports and detect dynamic loading, retaining explicit policy errors while removing the regex tokenizer.

candidates.title: Eight selectors require a 450-line custom glob-policy theorem prover
candidates.problemSummary: A 450-line builder plus 266-line policy with custom family trees, approximate disjointness proofs, and an escape hatch supports only 8 selectors. It replaces one ESLint ordering hazard with a repository-specific glob language that makes routine policy extension unusually difficult.
candidates.directionSummary: Compose over a small set of explicit named scopes, or generate a concrete flat-config partition from declarative scope membership, retaining the resolution snapshot as the behavior oracle.

candidates.title: Concurrency policy is fragmented across generated data, the lint rule, and the codemod
candidates.problemSummary: One logical concurrency change spans a generator input, generated graph, lint implementation, codemod scanner, helper-shape inventory, and two duplicated suggestion tables. The generated artifact covers only relation structure.
candidates.directionSummary: Define one generated concurrency-policy descriptor containing structural gates and repair metadata, consumed by both the lint rule and codemod scanner, preserving the deliberately separate corpora.

candidates.title: Generic codemod infrastructure is hidden behind a tRPC-specific grab bag
candidates.problemSummary: Reusable codemod foundations (errors, ts-morph setup, preview/write orchestration, import fixing) live inside tRPC-named modules. Unrelated codemods must import their infrastructure through a domain-specific barrel.
candidates.directionSummary: Extract focused codemod-core modules for errors, project construction, import normalization, and write/preview orchestration, leaving tRPC candidate and schema logic in the domain family.

candidates.title: Engine context leaves local-rule and cache layout hard-coded inside the kernel
candidates.problemSummary: The public engine context parameterizes repo root and data filenames but hard-codes local rules at eslint-rules/ and caches under node_modules/.cache/eslint-ratchet. The cache convention is reconstructed independently in two modules.
candidates.directionSummary: Extend the engine binding with local-rule resolution and a cache root or injected path functions, then centralize config and cache path construction.

candidates.title: The ratchet CLI has no authoritative command catalog
candidates.problemSummary: Fourteen CLI modes are hand-synchronized across five files totaling 963 lines (parser, types, validation, help, dispatch, preflight). No single descriptor owns a command's spelling, options, handler, or validation level.
candidates.directionSummary: Introduce a typed command catalog owning mode names, option grammar, validation and preflight policy, usage fragments, and handlers, deriving the duplicated unions and dispatch tables from it.

candidates.title: The metric strategy registry does not make metric additions registration-only
candidates.problemSummary: Despite the module's registration-only promise, adding a metric still requires closed-union, parser, validation, item-schema, and rule-pairing edits. An unused strategy enumerator makes the abstraction look more complete than it is.
candidates.directionSummary: Define one typed metric descriptor table supplying parsing, codec, comparison, merge, and rule-pairing metadata, and either expose an intentional extension seam or state that metrics are closed-world.

candidates.title: Fixture copies are parsed and grouped by two independent shell models
candidates.problemSummary: The shell-source closure and the sandbox model independently tokenize and resolve the same cp commands. Supporting another cp spelling, loop/glob form, or helper case requires keeping both models aligned.
candidates.directionSummary: Produce one canonical stream of parsed copy facts, or derive shell-only copy groups from the richer sandbox model while preserving the distinct closure policies.

candidates.title: The path-policy query core is closed over Musi's generated smoke registry
candidates.problemSummary: The query engine statically imports Musi's concrete policy, process-based smoke discovery, and a 913-line generated smoke registry even though only 2 of its 22 query names are smoke queries. The apparent data/engine boundary is not reusable.
candidates.directionSummary: Split the pure selector/query engine from a thin Musi adapter, injecting policy and smoke-subject resolution so non-smoke consumers avoid the generated registry.

candidates.title: Global restricted-import policy survives only through five manual restatements
candidates.problemSummary: Because flat config replaces rule values, every scoped no-restricted-imports block must manually re-copy the global schemas-barrel fence (five restatements counted). A new scoped policy can silently erase the repository-wide invariant.
candidates.directionSummary: Give the global fence its own local rule, or introduce an additive restricted-import composer so scoped policies cannot accidentally replace it.

candidates.title: The local-rule authoring contract exists only as repeated raw ESLint objects
candidates.problemSummary: All 32 production rule modules hand-copy ESLint metadata, message declarations, and schema/default handling (30 repeat schema: []). Omissions are found only indirectly by meta-checks and no authoring API parallels the centralized test factory.
candidates.directionSummary: Introduce a small JSDoc-typed defineLocalRule factory owning the Musi metadata contract and option/default plumbing, then migrate rules mechanically.

candidates.title: The concurrency guard compresses two analyzers and their orchestration into one rule
candidates.problemSummary: The 562-line rule interleaves direct-write and nested-write detectors that have different authority, aliases, corpora, and messages into one create function. Changing either branch requires understanding the entire hotspot.
candidates.directionSummary: Keep one public rule and separate corpora but extract direct-write and nested-write analyzers behind narrow alias and result interfaces.

candidates.title: Transaction callback tracking is duplicated between two local rules
candidates.problemSummary: Two rules independently implement transaction-callback discovery, alias tracking, and lifecycle state machines. Extending alias or callback syntax requires parallel edits that must stay aligned.
candidates.directionSummary: Extract a focused transaction-callback tracker supplying entry, exit, and transaction-client identity to both rules without a general classification framework.

candidates.title: Normal-lint probing is fragmented across fake configs and duplicate ESLint runners
candidates.problemSummary: Governance workflows needing normal-lint evidence each own a different mixture of config synthesis, file discovery, ESLint construction, and output parsing. Policy changes require finding every variant.
candidates.directionSummary: Introduce one package-level normal-lint probe with injected config and file-selection policy, routing retirement and zero-baseline governance through it.

candidates.title: The hook edit-check protocol is maintained manually in TypeScript and shell
candidates.problemSummary: Positional tab-separated wire formats span package TypeScript and shell consumers with no machine-readable shared contract; only some rows are decoded. Producer/consumer drift is detected late and the pattern is hard to copy safely.
candidates.directionSummary: Use a versioned self-describing record or generate TypeScript codecs and shell field contracts from one schema; at minimum centralize all row layouts and decode every emitted form.

candidates.title: Lint-message evaluation records source provenance but never verifies it
candidates.problemSummary: Fixtures carry a git commit, path, and source range, but evaluation never binds the copied source to the named commit. Arbitrary source can be attributed to any valid SHA and reports label it as the evaluated commit.
candidates.directionSummary: Load the named path and range from gitCommit and require an exact source match, or explicitly model the trace as an unverified replay and remove or relabel the ceremonial metadata.

candidates.title: shared-policy.js is a grab bag for unrelated lint domains
candidates.problemSummary: One high-fan-in module simultaneously owns path vocabulary, test-runner registries, codemod inventory, package-boundary policy, and a stateful max-lines loader. Unrelated changes converge on a single file whose name suggests reusable policy.
candidates.directionSummary: Split it into focused config-surface, scripts-and-tests, package-boundary, and max-lines policy modules with direct imports rather than another barrel.

candidates.title: TypeScript consumers depend on a hand-written shadow of checked JavaScript policy
candidates.problemSummary: Runtime lint policy lives in checked JavaScript while 10 TypeScript consumers compile against a 113-line hand-maintained ambient declaration of five wildcard modules. Contributors must synchronize semantic types across three surfaces.
candidates.directionSummary: Generate declarations from the checked JavaScript/JSDoc contract or establish one declaration-emitting policy-data boundary consumed by both ESLint config and TypeScript scripts, keeping only a thin binding if resolution requires it.

candidates.title: Path-policy gives single-segment glob two incompatible private grammars
candidates.problemSummary: Within one module family, the same single-segment-glob vocabulary denotes different languages: one matcher escapes brackets, another passes them into RegExp semantics, and loop parsing separately rejects glob-shaped remainders. Contributors must discover per-implementation punctuation rules.
candidates.directionSummary: Define one documented segment-pattern codec and matcher, or give deliberately narrower dialects distinct types and names, sharing with lint-coverage machinery only where semantics match.

candidates.title: Bulk codemod modes write one target at a time instead of building one plan
candidates.problemSummary: The --all modes loop over independently writing single-target operations, repeatedly constructing projects and scanning files. Intermediate repository states are exposed and per-target recovery reasoning replaces one reviewable plan.
candidates.directionSummary: Separate analysis from commit: one project, validate every target, merge plans with collision detection, and invoke the shared writer once after the complete bulk plan succeeds.

candidates.title: The debt-log union uses the absence of a discriminator as an entry kind
candidates.problemSummary: Accepted-debt entries are the only persisted variant without a kind field and are recognized indirectly via acceptanceReason. Adding an entry kind requires coordinated schema, predicate, parser, classification, and rendering edits without exhaustive dispatch.
candidates.directionSummary: Write new accepted-debt records with an explicit kind, isolate compatibility parsing for existing kind-less version-1 lines, and dispatch normalized records through exhaustive kind switches.

candidates.title: Suppression allowlists cannot ratchet downward
candidates.problemSummary: Both suppression registers check only forward membership and never fail on allowlist rows whose suppressions disappeared. The @ts-nocheck allowlist is already fully stale (0 of 2 rows live), leaving standing permission to reintroduce file-wide suppression.
candidates.directionSummary: During full scans, track which allowlist rows match live directives and fail on unused rows, preserving the existing scan and glob formats and limiting stale-row validation to full-scan scope.

candidates.title: The drift-ai executable exposes an incoherent 23-module pseudo-API
candidates.problemSummary: The drift-ai executable selectively re-exports 23 internal module paths as an ad hoc programmatic API with no inclusion rule, zero production importers, and only test consumers. Maintainers must preserve a second manual boundary.
candidates.directionSummary: Keep the executable as a narrow delegation shell and, if a programmatic surface is required, define it explicitly in a side-effect-free drift-ai API module with intentional exports and compatibility guarantees.

candidates.title: Logs-audit leaves its ingestion core in the flat executable
candidates.problemSummary: The logs-audit analyzer is split at an arbitrary boundary: checks, formatting, and types live under logs-audit/ while option parsing, JSONL ingestion, report merging, and run orchestration remain in the side-effect-bearing flat executable.
candidates.directionSummary: Move argument handling, JSONL ingestion, report merging, and run orchestration into focused logs-audit modules, leaving the flat file as a small executable delegate with only genuinely consumed re-exports.
